Malinin has won seven Grand Prix events in a row overall, a run dating to 2023. His top challengers this week include Italian Daniel Grassl, who was ninth at the Olympics and fourth at each of the last two Grand Prix Finals. Two-time U.S. champions Alisa Efimova and Misha Mitrofanov have a shot to qualify for their first Grand Prix Final (Dec. 10-13 in China). They likely need a podium at Skate America for a realistic chance, two weeks after placing second at Skate Canada. item.title: Alexis Mac Allister shares what one Crystal Palace player told him about Alisson on Sunday
item.description: Alexis Mac Allister shares what one Crystal Palace player told him about Alisson on Sunday Alisson Becker’s outstanding performance in Liverpool’s 3-1 win away to Crystal Palace on Sunday was reflected in what one Eagles player told Alexis Mac Allister. The Reds’ number 1 had shipped criticism in recent days for errors in the defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce , but he was back to his world-class best at Selhurst Park yesterday as he turned in a man-of-the-match display for his side. The Brazilian pulled off six saves in total against Pierre Sage’s team, including a stunning reaction stop to keep out a fearsome volley from Daichi Kamada just a couple of minutes before the Argentine scored the visitors’ opening goal. Kamada left in awe of Alisson’s brilliance Speaking to BBC Sport after the match (via liverpoolfc.com ), Mac Allister was singing Alisson’s praises and shared what the Japan international had told him about the Liverpool goalkeeper. The Reds’ number 10 said of the Brazil stopper: “He’s so good, especially the save from Kamada’s shot [in the first half]. Kamada couldn’t believe the save he made and he was telling me, but that’s who he is. “He is an amazing goalkeeper and an amazing guy as well. I’m really, really happy for him.” Image via Sky Sports Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Alisson reminds us of his world-class brilliance Alisson had endured some unusually shaky moments in recent weeks, but he reminded us all on Sunday that class is permanent and that he remains pivotal to Liverpool’s hopes of success this season. In addition to the outstanding save from Kamada, he also produced excellent stops to keep out an Adam Wharton header just before half-time and a double save from Yeremy Pino and Jefferson Lerma in the 77th minute when the Reds were 2-0 to the good. That Palace scored just once from an xG of 2.6 yesterday sums up just how imperious our number 1 had been, and it’s no wonder that the Eagles’ Japanese attacker was stunned by the 34-year-old’s brilliance. Such was Alisson’s performance at Selhurst Park that the Premier League’s official X profile posted a compilation of his saves from the win over the south London outfit, with the goalkeeper treating us to his own showreel. Anyone who might’ve thought that the Brazil international was in irreversible decline was made to think again yesterday by a masterclass from Liverpool’s legendary number 1.

item.title: Blue Jays predicted to sign $85M Gold Glove finalist to fill major need left by George Springer
item.description: Blue Jays predicted to sign $85M Gold Glove finalist to fill major need left by George Springer originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays were one of the more disappointing teams of the 2026 season, especially after making a World Series appearance the year before. It was a season in which the roster was decimated by injuries. They will enter the offseason with an obvious goal of competing for some of the biggest free agents on the market. One name the Blue Jays are already interested in is Seiya Suzuki. “The Blue Jays didn't make the playoffs this year, so they are already in offseason mode. Mitch Bannon of The Athletic reports that the Jays are expected to pursue outfielder Seiya Suzuki when he hits free agency about a month from now," MLB Trade Rumors' Darragh McDonald wrote. The reason for this interest is that Toronto needs an outfielder who can produce at an All-Star level. The Blue Jays must find someone who can provide production similar to George Springer, who is likely retiring. “It's been a long time since the Blue Jays developed an All-Star-caliber outfielder. You're stuck reaching for Kevin Pillar's peak seasons, then even further for Vernon Wells, who last played for the Blue Jays in 2010. Essentially, the Blue Jays need to find their next George Springer," MLB.com's Keegan Matheson wrote. Sports Illustrated’s Will Laws believes the Blue Jays will sign Suzuki this winter. “Yes, it’s a down year for bats if Suzuki is our top-ranked hitter with MLB experience. That being said, he was nothing if not consistent with the Cubs, averaging 25 home runs with something between 140 and 147 hits over the last four years with a .833 OPS, never registering a wRC+ below 123. He also logged a career-high .368 on-base percentage in 2026 and improved in a major way on defense, recording 14 defensive runs saved after never previously topping two to be honored as a Gold Glove finalist for the first time,” Laws wrote. Suzuki is coming off a very good season in which he proved he can contribute beyond his offensive production. The right fielder was also named a Gold Glove finalist, and that recognition was backed by his defensive performance. Suzuki previously played under an $85 million contract with the Chicago Cubs. He has a cannon for an arm in right field and has been a consistent offensive contributor, even earning Silver Slugger finalist recognition just a couple of seasons ago. This is the type of move the Blue Jays would love to make. item.description: Gasperini: “I used to be the enemy, now we’re writing a beautiful chapter together.” Gian Piero Gasperini received the fifth annual “Cuore di Leone-Gian Luigi Corti” award at Genoa’s Porto Antico. The Giallorossi coach commented on Inter’s victory over Como: “We know that Inter is a great team, but so is Como, in a championship that is proving to be truly balanced.” These are his comments, reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. The general from Grugliasco commented on his happy moment with Roma: “My story with Roma is still young, having begun a year and a half ago, but it’s as wonderful as the previous ones. We hope to continue on this path.” The coach of the Roman club on Lazio’s start to the season: “It’s certainly a surprise, but it also represents value and recognition for the city. Rome is extraordinary, even in terms of enthusiasm for football. Roma always has a full stadium, while Lazio perhaps has other problems.” Regarding the successes and solidity of his group, Gasperini gave an initial assessment of this season: “We have been competitive for a few months now. Roma has improved a lot, but we started well last year too. Eleven games is certainly not a lot, but it is still significant for how the team has performed. The environment gives us great fuel to do well.” The Giallorossi coach concluded with what motivated him to accept the move to the capital: “When my time with Atalanta ended, I went to a club I was a bitter enemy of. It wasn’t exactly a respected opponent, but it was also a great challenge. I was convinced that Roma was the club with the greatest football enthusiasm. It was a great challenge, and challenge and courage go well together.”

item.title: What happens in Vegas? Top MLB free agents and trade targets for GM Meetings
item.description: LAS VEGAS — They’re arriving from all parts of the country like every other tourist hitting the casinos, hoping their wager strikes it rich so they can a fortune back home. Some spinning roulette wheels. And others flipping cards at the blackjack or rolling dice at the craps tables. But for executives representing the 30 teams arriving into town Monday for Major League Baseball’s General Manager meetings , they’ll be trying to sweet-talk free agents, coerce rivals into trades, and hope to leave town by the end of the week with at least one desired possession on their radar. These meetings will be unique with no executive or agent knowing exactly how the landscape will look like in 2027. Will there be a salary cap? Will there be strict financial restrictions? Will nothing be changed? Will everything look different? When will the 2027 season start? Will there even be a 2027 season ? MLB HOT STOVE: Ranking top 112 free agents: Will Tarik Skubal sign before lockout? The best bet is that the high-priced free agents, fearing the great unknown, will sign before the pending lockout at 11:59 p.m ET on Dec. 1, to get their money now while big-market teams still are in play. This means no more waltzing through the winter and all of the way until spring training, with players wanting to secure their future in these next three weeks before the lockout, just like 2021 when nearly $2 billion was spent in the final days before the 99-day lockout. There were six free-agent signings in excess of $100 million that year, with the Texas Rangers dropping a cool $500 million on infielders Corey Seager and Marcus Semien, and a record 27 signings in all the final day. But this weak free-agent class, sorely lacking in depth, could mean that teams will be more aggressive in trade talks, believing their best hope is to part with prospects instead of relying on checkbook baseball. Yet, with the lockout potentially shortening the 2027 season, GMs believe that players with only one more year of control will have their value diminished unknowing just how many games he’ll actually play for his new team. GMs and executives believe the blueprint for these meetings will be eerily similar to 2021. item.title: Gavi has cheeky praise for Frenkie de Jong after Barcelona beat Atletico Madrid
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 08: Pablo Martin "Gavi" of FC Barcelona celebrates victory after the game the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between Atletico de Madrid and FC Barcelona at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 08, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona midfielder Gavi had some cheeky words of praise for Frenkie de Jong following his performance in the 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday. De Jong came on at half-time at right-back before moving into midfield as Barcelona secured an important win that keeps them top of the table over the international break. Gavi was asked about Frenkie afterwards and was happy to shower his team-mate with praise. “Frenkie is very good, the bastard, and he can play a lot of different positions,” he told Catalunya Radio. “Today he showed that again. He is a team player and he did very well and we are very happy with the performance he had.” The midfielder, who also featured as a substitute in the second half, also spoke about his delight at beating Diego Simeone’s side. “It was a very important victory for us. It was a crucial match for the team, and we’re very happy to have won. They had chances, but this is about scoring goals. We knew how to take advantage of our opportunities, and we’re proud to win today. It’s a team victory,” he explained. “We dominated the second half very well. We managed the game well, which is important for us young players. We’ve improved in many aspects. I’m very happy for the team. “Atletico have the weapons to do us a lot of damage. These matches against Atlético are difficult. They’re like a war because the atmosphere is intense, the most intense in Europe. It was very important for us to get the victory.”

item.title: Warriors predicted to trade Draymond Green for ex-No. 1 pick, 2x All-Star to pair with Steph Curry
item.description: Warriors predicted to trade Draymond Green for ex-No. 1 pick, 2x All-Star to pair with Steph Curry originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Before the season began, much of the attention surrounding the Golden State Warriors was focused on Steph Curry and whether the two sides would agree to a contract extension. Curry has led the organization for well over a decade, becoming the face of the franchise. Curry finishing his career in the Bay Area means a great deal to the Golden State organization and its fans. That's why his latest extension is so significant , as it will likely be the final one of his career. “Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, tying the franchise legend to the only organization he has ever known through his 20th NBA season, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday. The deal includes a player option in the final season (2028-29), according to sources," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. The season didn't get off to a great start for Golden State. In fact, early struggles made it appear as though the Warriors could be in for a long year. However, the team has turned things around, and some believe rookie phenom Yaxel Lendeborg has helped save the Curry era. “Yaxel might have single-handedly saved the Steph era, like for real, and I can't tell you how good he was in this Denver game last night . . . Yaxel looked like mid-2010's LeBron in this game. I don't say that lightly because mid-2010's LeBron was awesome. They're running the offense through him. He was all over the place on defense. He was rebounding. He was initiating stuff. He was getting to the basket whenever. It was unbelievable. I couldn't believe it. I couldn't believe how good he was," Bill Simmons said. With the Warriors looking to make another championship run alongside Curry, some believe the organization should pursue one last trip to the NBA Finals. Bleacher Report's Andy Bailey proposed a trade that would send Draymond Green, Kristaps Porziņģis and a top-four-protected 2027 first-round pick to the New Orleans Pelicans in exchange for Zion Williamson. “Trading one health risk for another is not ideal. Surrendering a precious draft asset in the process makes it even less so. And prior to recent news on Porziņģis, Zion was arguably the biggest health risk in the league (with tongue-in-cheek apologies to KP and Joel Embiid). But in this point in their careers, Zion would represent a massive talent upgrade over Draymond. And whatever that swap would cost Golden State defensively, Williamson could offset it on the other end,” Bailey wrote. This would certainly be an interesting deal, but it could pay off in a major way if Williamson stays healthy. It would also open a roster spot for Golden State to potentially add another player through the buyout market. Williamson is currently playing under a $197 million contract with the Pelicans.

item.title: Hansi Flick closes in on Guardiola and Cruyff with historic Barcelona comeback record
item.description: Hansi Flick closes in on Guardiola and Cruyff with historic Barcelona comeback record Hansi Flick is closing in on two of Barcelona’s most celebrated managers after guiding his side to a 2-1 comeback victory over Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano. Notably, the result took the German to 23 comeback wins in 133 matches in charge of Barça , leaving him just one behind Pep Guardiola and five short of Johan Cruyff in the club’s historical ranking. Flick approaches Guardiola and Cruyff in Barcelona’s record books As noted, Cruyff leads the ranking with 28 comeback victories from 430 matches as Barcelona manager, while Guardiola recorded 24 in 249 games. Flick, on his part, has already registered 23 in only 133 appearances. Under the German coach, Barcelona have won 21 of the 42 matches in which they have fallen behind, giving the German a 50% conversion rate in those situations. Fermin completes Barcelona’s turnaround against Atletico The latest addition came at the Metropolitano, where Barcelona had to overcome an early setback. Giuliano Simeone put Atletico ahead in the 10th minute, following an opening period in which Julian Alvarez had already threatened Barcelona’s goal. Fermin Lopez restored parity just before half-time with a left-footed finish after Pedri created the opportunity. Barcelona returned with greater intensity after the interval, and their improvement was rewarded in the 66th minute when Lamine Yamal supplied Fermin for his second goal. A significant milestone in Flick’s Barcelona tenure Barcelona had to work hard to beat Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The Atletico victory was Barcelona’s fourth comeback win of the season, following their results against Rayo Vallecano, Sevilla and Galatasaray. Indeed, apart from the obvious three points, the result preserved Barcelona’s advantage over Real Madrid at the top of La Liga and left Atletico five points behind, while also bringing a historic managerial comparison within reach for Flick. For now, Guardiola’s 24 victories are the next benchmark. Cruyff remains ahead, but Flick’s progress after only 133 matches has already made his place among Barcelona’s most successful comeback managers a strong part of his tenure.

item.title: Everton keen on move for MLS star
item.description: Everton keen on move for MLS star Everton Transfer Interest in Kelvin Yeboah Grows as Leeds United Step Back Everton’s search for attacking reinforcements appears to have taken on extra significance, with The Hard Tackle reporting fresh context around Kelvin Yeboah’s situation and Leeds United’s current stance. The 26-year-old Minnesota United forward has put together an eye-catching campaign in MLS, recording 18 goals in 32 appearances and further strengthening a profile that has started to attract attention on both sides of the Atlantic. Inevitably, that has prompted discussion about a possible return to European football, particularly given his prior experience across several major leagues. Any mention of Leeds United naturally carried added intrigue because of the family link. Tony Yeboah remains an iconic figure at Elland Road, and Kelvin Yeboah’s surname ensures the story writes itself to a degree. Yet Leeds are not expected to be moved by sentiment. Their focus is understood to be elsewhere, with other positions taking precedence as planning continues for the next window. Photo: IMAGO Everton striker search gathers pace That development sharpens attention on Everton. David Moyes is light on recognised senior centre-forward options, and the need for depth in that department looks obvious. In that context, Yeboah stands out as a player of genuine interest rather than one of many loosely connected names. There is a practical element to the appeal. Yeboah’s contract runs until December 2027, which creates a scenario in which Minnesota may soon have to think carefully about value protection. By the time the winter market opens, Everton could see room to test the conditions of a deal and assess whether the financials line up with their wider recruitment priorities. For Everton, this would be a decision shaped by more than raw output. Yeboah has played in Serie A, the Bundesliga, Ligue 1 and Belgium, which offers reassurance that he has operated in demanding environments before. At the same time, his spells outside Italy have not always delivered complete consistency, so internal checks would be essential before any move progressed. Kelvin Yeboah form demands attention Still, the numbers are increasingly difficult to dismiss. item.title: The moment Mercedes’ glorious F1 comeback started? How about their lowest-ever ebb
item.description: “One of my worst days in racing,” proclaimed an aghast Toto Wolff . The scene is the paddock at the Bahrain International Circuit, the date is March 2023 and the occasion is the aftermath of the season-opening Formula 1 race. Mercedes have just finished more than 50 seconds off the pace set by winner Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, with Lewis Hamilton in fifth and George Russell in seventh. Behind three other cars, the former untouchable giants of Formula 1 are, clearly, the fourth-quickest car on the grid . And in that moment, Wolff realises that – once again – he and his team of engineers and car designers back at their Brackley base have got it badly wrong. It’s worth revisiting the Silver Arrows at their lowest ebb as we revert back to the present day. On Sunday, Mercedes claimed the F1 constructors’ crown for the first time in five years, a week on from their first drivers’ world championship in six years. It is a ninth teams’ title for Mercedes, putting them level with Williams and placing them one behind McLaren on the all-time list. For Wolff, too, it puts him level with Frank Williams for the most titles for a team boss in F1 history. Mercedes celebrate in Sao Paulo (Bradley Collyer/PA) (PA Wire) Not bad, then, given the desperate doldrums the Austrian executive found himself in nearly four years ago. That day in Bahrain marked the start of this new era. A year earlier, amid the new ground-effect rule change off the back of that 2021 decider in Abu Dhabi , Mercedes’ zero-sidepod design caught the attention of everyone up and down the pit-lane. And yet, as action began on the track, not only were they short of top-table pace, but their car was violently oscillating in a phenomenon called “porpoising” that nobody at HQ had envisaged. So much so that, after one race in Baku, Hamilton struggled to disembark the cockpit, such was the pain in his back. But Russell’s inaugural victory in Formula 1 at Interlagos – Mercedes’ first win of the 2022 season, on a weekend where they claimed a one-two finish – presented a lifeline. Or so they thought at the time. Wolff has since acknowledged that it was that win which pushed Mercedes to continue down the zero-sidepod path. In a holistic game of stick-and-twist – with a rule phase not ending until 2026 – the three-pronged star decided to stick. It would prove to be a foolhardy decision. Despite seven grands prix triumphs between 2023-2025, Mercedes were still someway short of their competitors: first Red Bull, then McLaren. The three years since were something of a purgatory for Wolff who, to his credit, has never been one for hiding his emotions or ducking out of camera range in the garage, often to the detriment of a nearby headset. "Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation’ – but when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel,” he said on Sunday night, another constructors’ title in his back pocket. item.description: FBL-FRA-FRIENDLY-LENS-SUNDERLAND - AFP Lens defender Ismaelo Ganiou is attracting interest from Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Chelsea owners BlueCo and Manchester City's parent group after his Ligue 1 breakthrough. The highly rated youngster has drawn comparisons to former Bollaert-Delelis graduate Raphael Varane as European heavyweights track his rise. English clubs monitor French prospect According to TEAMtalk , Premier League duo Fulham and Brentford have joined Tottenham and Newcastle in scouting Ganiou throughout 2026 following his impressive emergence in French football. Meanwhile, multi-club ownership groups BlueCo and City Football Group have also been keeping close tabs on the central defender's progress. Officials at his current employers hope the homegrown talent can emulate former France and Real Madrid star Varane. Continental suitors track academy graduate The report states that domestic rivals Paris Saint-Germain, Marseille and Monaco are all fully aware of the defender's burgeoning potential and have been monitoring his top-flight displays closely over recent months. Significant interest has also spread across the continent, with German Bundesliga outfits Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig tracking his development alongside Italian Serie A pair Atalanta and Como. Much like Varane, who is widely regarded as the northern French club's greatest-ever youth product, the sought-after youngster combines impressive recovery pace and elegance in possession with physical toughness. Those standout attributes have quickly established him among the most promising young central defenders in Ligue 1 after he progressed through the youth ranks in northern France. Unorthodox pathway precedes contract reward However, the outlet notes that his pathway into the senior side was far from straightforward due to complex administrative restrictions surrounding loan registrations. His rapid progression subsequently convinced the club's hierarchy to tie him down to a new four-year contract over the summer in a move that reflects their belief in his ability. International switch boosts growing reputation Born in Lille, Ganiou initially represented Burkina Faso in a 2025 friendly against Zimbabwe through his parents' heritage before switching allegiance to France Under-21s in March. item.title: "I'm involved in 50 percent of his goals" – Hoeneß makes bold Karl claim after criticism
item.description: "I'm involved in 50 percent of his goals" – Hoeneß makes bold Karl claim after criticism Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeneß made headlines just over two weeks ago when he criticised youngster Lennart Karl for lacking humility and revealed plans to have a serious conversation with the teenager following a dip in performances. "I'm involved in 50 percent of his goals," Hoeneß said with a smile, adding that he sees it as his responsibility to guide young players. “We have a duty to show young players the way,” he added. "I have so much experience. But if a young player doesn't listen to me, then I have to stop." In his criticism of Karl, Hoeneß took aim at the youngster's use of social media, reflecting his wider concerns about its influence on young players. "Social media is the biggest problem," he said, describing the world of influencers as a "cesspit". The Bayern honorary president believes young players, in particular, can quickly lose sight of what really matters amid the constant attention and self-promotion on social media. “I have to do something about that. item.title: Ali weeps as world title dream realised in Texas
item.description: Ramla Ali was the first boxer from Somalia to compete at an Olympics [Getty Images] Ramla Ali secured her first world title at the age of 36 after defeating Mikiah Kreps in a split-decision victory in Arlington, Texas. The win is a crowning moment for the Briton, who fled a war-torn Somalia as a child before going on to become an Olympian, activist, author and now the WBO and IBF super-bantamweight champion. With her biopic about her remarkable life just released, Ali fulfilled a dream long in the making and that seemed far away when she was swept aside by Yamileth Mercado in her first attempt two years ago. An emotional Ali fell to her knees in tears as she was confirmed the winner with scorecards that read 97-92, 96-93 and 98-91 in her favour, dedicating the victory to her late father. "When we were in the changing room, my coach said, because my dad passed away in May, 'Do this for him'," Ali said. "That's where those emotions came out at the end, because I did it for my dad." "I can't put into words what this means to me and what this means to all of Somalia," she added. "I've hopefully inspired so many young girls and boys out there to dream big and that's all I've ever wanted to do." As Ali wept, there was devastation for Kreps who was convinced she had done enough to win the contest. The previously undefeated American suffered a knockdown in the third round, walking onto a flush left hook from Ali. Kreps was unhappy with the knockdown call but replays showed the heavy shot caused the 30-year-old's glove to touch the canvas as she tried to steady herself. With a 10-8 round in the bag, Ali was unable to build on the moment, having to stand firm as Kreps came storming back and applying constant pressure. Kreps outlanded Ali with 115 punches to 78 and secured 91 power shots to Ali's 70 and one judge certainly was convinced of her as a clear winner with a wide 98-91 scorecard. With the fight threatening to slip away from her in the second half, Ali said every round was a mental battle to rise from her stool. "I remember going to the corner every round and I remember saying 'I'm so tired, I can't do this'. All my coach responded was 'think about your dad, do this for your dad'. I think that really pushed me. I really boxed out of my skin, I was so knackered. I did it for him," Ali said. "Every time I went to the corner, I kept saying, 'I'm so tired. I'm so tired,' because your work rate was just next level." What next for trailblazer Ali? With two world titles secured, Ali could set her sights on an intriguing unification bout with Skye Nicolson after the Australia kept hold of her WBC belt on the undercard. Nicolson is also signed to Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions and beat Japan's Miyo Yoshida by unanimous decision. But Ali will for now celebrate her victory as she delivered yet another high point in an incredible life that might have seen as impossible when her family escaped Somalia when she was just a baby. item.title: Johnston completes undefeated season with a long-awaited first title
item.description: PROVIDENCE – Make that one less boys soccer program in the state waiting for a first championship. Johnston is off the list after completing an undefeated season Sunday night, November 8, a coronation in Division III at Rhode Island College. Darrell Acosta gave the Panthers a lead early in the second half and Jayden Corrales iced the result with a brilliant free kick late. Johnston eased to a 2-0 win over Ponaganset, one that finally delivered the school a long-awaited crown. The Panthers debuted in 1973, didn't field a team from 1985-89 and counted just four winning seasons until 2018. Johnston closed with finals defeats in 2020 and 2024 before this breakthrough, rolling through 21 league matches without suffering a loss. Central, Cumberland and Woonsocket are now a trio after the Panthers escaped some unwanted territory. "We were fully aware coming into the season that we needed to get this," Johnston captain Andre Amato said. "We needed to make history, and we just did. I'm so proud of our team." Johnston had a couple good chances in the opening half but still was locked in a 0-0 draw at the break. The Panthers needed less than two minutes after the restart to take command, and it was Acosta producing some trademark brilliance. He took possession in his own half, slipped his way past three defenders and fired a deflected shot that crawled its way over the line to make it 1-0. "Darrell is such a special player," Amato said. "We were so happy to have him on the team once he joined two years ago. I think everyone thanks him for the season as well." Pedro Saucedo parried a shot over the crossbar in the 54 th minute, denying the Chieftains what turned out to be their best chance to draw level. Johnston eventually put away some insurance when Corrales took aim with a free kick from the left side in the 79 th minute. His curling right-footed shot ripped into the top corner, and the Panthers were able to start the celebration early. "The best goal I've ever scored," Corrales said. "The best goal I've ever scored in my career." Watch RI games on NFHS Network! Ponaganset (13-4-4) was looking to add just a second championship to the Division II crown it secured in 1982. The Chieftains took care of Blackstone Valley Prep in the quarterfinals and beat Exeter-West Greenwich, 3-1, in the semifinals. The Scarlet Knights and Johnston were the last two unbeatens in the league standings – that result raised an eyebrow or two. The Panthers (18-0-3) eased past Woonsocket in the quarterfinals before some trouble in their own semifinal. Acosta scored twice and dished out an assist in a 3-1 win, but a fight with 5:18 left cost Johnston four players and coach Yevegen Fedorchuk for this title round. item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following trip finale win over Bulls
item.description: CHICAGO -- The Philadelphia 76ers finished their 3-game road trip with a 127-121 win over the Chicago Bulls on Sunday afternoon to go 2-1 on the trip. The Sixers are now 9-2 on the season after handling business against a rebuilding, but scrappy Bulls team in a hostile United Center. LeBron James had 22 points, five rebounds, and five assists for Philadelphia while Tyrese Maxey had 27 points and seven assists, and Jaylen Brown had 29 points, seven rebounds, and four assists. Joel Embiid had 18 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists, and VJ Edgecombe had 13 and six rebounds. Jabari Walker was fantastic off the bench with nine and 11 boards and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope added six, six rebounds, and three assists. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the win: Big night for Walker Of Walker's 11 rebounds, five of them were on the offensive glass. He was fantastic in a number of ways for the Sixers and he gave them a big spark. One could argue Philadelphia doesn't win this game unless Walker steps in and provides the lift he gave on the glass. He created so many extra possessions for the Sixers, and even if he didn't grab the offensive rebound himself, he tapped it away in order to keep it away from the Bulls and allow his teammates to crash and come up with the ball. This is the perfect night for a backup center and his team certainly appreciated his efforts against Chicago. "He’s continuing to do kind of the same thing," said coach Nick Nurse. "He’s playing hard. He had five offensive rebounds and probably another five near misses. When he’s in there, it’s such a hard defensive rebound for them, it slows transition. So those are like, kind of, impactful plays too. And again, finishing at the basket, and throwing in a 3. They are very very good minutes." James' big second quarter After such a miserable game in Cleveland on Friday, James responded in a big way in this one with the season-high in points. The future Hall of Famer helped Philadelphia seize control of the game in the second when he scored 13 points on 5-for-9 shooting, including knocking down two triples, and just imposing his will on the game the way James has done so many times in his career. He has taken a step back with his scoring a bit as he looks to fit in with his new team, but James gave a big lift against the Bulls on Sunday. "I’m happy he started the game that way," Nurse stated. The 43-year-old was also Aston Villa’s caretaker head coach before Unai Emery’s arrival. “United believe his coaching qualities could prove valuable if they decide to give their current manager further backing,” the report states. The possibility of bringing in Danks or another coach to improve Carrick ‘s staff is reportedly just one of many avenues being considered by Wilcox and Omar Berrada.
